info.title: Tracker API
info.description:
REST API for Tracker, a self-hosted agile project tracker. Everything the web app does goes through this API.

## Authentication

Every user has an **API token** (Profile → API token, or `GET /api/v1/me`). Send it on each request:

```
curl -H "X-TrackerToken: $TOKEN" https://tracker.example.com/api/v1/projects
```

`Authorization: Bearer <token>` also works. Browsers use a session cookie set by `POST /auth/login`.

## Conventions

* JSON in, JSON out. Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC; calendar dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* Every resource has a `kind` field (`story`, `project`, …).
* `PUT` performs partial updates: omitted fields are unchanged. List-valued fields (`owner_ids`, `label_ids`, …) replace the whole list.
* Unknown body fields are ignored.

## Pagination

List endpoints accept `limit` and `offset` and return these headers:
`X-Tracker-Pagination-Total`, `X-Tracker-Pagination-Limit`, `X-Tracker-Pagination-Offset`, `X-Tracker-Pagination-Returned`.

## Errors

Errors use a consistent envelope with an HTTP 4xx/5xx status:

```json
{ "kind": "error", "code": "invalid_parameter", "error": "Unestimated feature stories cannot be started.",
  "possible_fix": "Give the story an estimate first." }
```

Codes: `invalid_parameter` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `unauthorized_operation` (403), `unfound_resource` (404),
`conflict` (409), `request_too_large` (413), `too_many_requests` (429), `server_error` (500).

## Story workflow

```
unscheduled (icebox) → unstarted → started → finished → delivered → accepted
                                                              ↘ rejected → started …
```
Chores go `started → accepted`. Releases go `unstarted → accepted`. Features need an estimate before they can be started.

## Planning

Stories share one priority order per project (`position`). Reorder with `before_id`/`after_id` on `PUT /stories/:id`.
Velocity is the average points accepted over the last `velocity_averaged_over` iterations (normalised for team strength and
iteration length). The current iteration and backlog are filled by velocity in priority order (see `GET /iterations`).

## Realtime & webhooks

`GET /api/v1/events` streams Server-Sent Events for the projects you subscribe to. Project webhooks POST every activity
as JSON, signed with `X-Tracker-Signature: sha256=HMAC_SHA256(secret, body)`.

## Version control

Reference stories in commit messages — `[#123]`, `[Finishes #123]`, `[Delivers #123]` — and send commits via
`POST /source_commits` or a repository push webhook to `/integrations/vcs?token=…`.

put.description:
Partial update. Notable behaviour:

* **State changes** enforce the workflow: unestimated features cannot be started; chores have no finished/delivered/rejected; releases only unstarted/accepted. Starting a story with no owners makes you the owner. Accepting sets `accepted_at`.
* **Prioritisation:** pass `before_id` or `after_id` to move the story. Move between icebox and backlog by also changing `current_state` (`unscheduled` ↔ `unstarted`).
* `owner_ids`, `follower_ids`, `label_ids`/`labels` replace the existing lists.
* Set `project_id` to move the story to another project.

get.description:
Iterations computed from velocity.

* `done`: completed iterations (accepted stories, bucketed by acceptance date). `limit`/`offset` count back from the most recent.
* `current`: the iteration containing today: accepted-this-iteration, in-progress, then as many unstarted stories as fit.
* `backlog`: future iterations projected by velocity (or by planned_iteration_number when automatic planning is off).
* `current_backlog`: both.

Pass `velocity` to see "what if" projections.

parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return

get.description: Everything needed to render the planning board in one request: project, current + backlog iterations (story ids), icebox ids, release projections, and all referenced stories. Done iterations are fetched separately via /iterations?scope=done.

Full query language: free text, "phrases", label:, type:, state:, owner:, requester:, follower:, reviewer:, mywork:, id:, estimate:, epic:, is:, has:, name:, description:, created_since:/created_before:, updated_since:/updated_before:, accepted_since:/accepted_before:, includedone:true. Prefix a filter with "-" to negate. Accepted stories are excluded unless includedone:true (or the query asks for them).
Newest first. Use `since_version` to fetch only changes after a known project version (useful for syncing).

One row per story in priority order. Multiple owners, comments and tasks appear as repeated columns.

post.description: Send CSV as `text/csv`, or JSON `{ "csv": "..." }`. Recognised columns (case-insensitive): Title (required), Type, Estimate, Current State, Labels, Description, Requested By, Owned By (repeatable), Deadline, Accepted at, Created at, Comment (repeatable), Task + Task Status (repeatable). People are matched by name, username or email among project members. Ids are ignored; stories are appended in file order. Compatible with exports from this server and other trackers using the same column names.

get.description: Workspaces are personal views that show several projects side by side.

Opens a `text/event-stream`. Subscribe to projects with `project_ids=1,2`; your own notifications are always included. Because browsers' EventSource cannot send headers, the API token may be passed as `?token=`.

Events:
* `activity` — data is an Activity (a project changed; refetch or apply).
* `notification` — data is a Notification for you.
* `project` — project-level events such as deletion.
* `ping` — keep-alive every 25 s.

post.description: Upload a file as `multipart/form-data` (field name `file`). Returns a file attachment that is not yet attached to anything; pass its id in `file_attachment_ids` when creating a comment. Unattached uploads are removed after 24 hours.

get.description: Streams the file. Images, PDFs, audio/video and plain text are served inline; other types as downloads. Accepts `?token=` for use in links.

delete.description: The uploader or a project owner can delete a file (it is removed from its comment).

post.description: Without a password, the user is invited and the response includes an `invite_url`.

put.description: Deactivated users cannot sign in or use the API; their history is kept.

delete.description: Removes the account and memberships. Stories and comments remain (attributed to nobody). Prefer deactivation.

post.description: For instances without email: share the link with the user. Valid for 24 hours.

Link a commit to stories. Reference stories in the message in square brackets: `[#123]` comments on the story, `[Finishes #123]` (or Fixes/Completes) also finishes it, `[Delivers #123]` delivers it. Several ids may share a bracket. Chores are accepted instead of finished. Stories are never moved backwards.

post.summary: GitHub / GitLab / Gitea / Bitbucket push webhook
post.description: Point a repository push webhook (content type application/json) at `/api/v1/integrations/vcs?token=<your API token>`. The provider is detected from its event header (`X-GitHub-Event`, `X-Gitlab-Event`, `X-Gitea-Event`, `X-Event-Key`); any other JSON body with a `commits: [{ id, message, url, author: { name } }]` array is also accepted. Each pushed commit is processed like POST /source_commits. Commits are attributed to the token owner, with the commit author shown in the comment. Non-push events (e.g. pings) are acknowledged with `processed: 0`.
